--- title: "Syllable counting" subtitle: "Automatically generated task sheet · CF_CONTAR_SILABAS" --- ::: {.callout-note appearance="minimal"} **Automatically generated task sheet** (A · Accuracy; quality class A). Generated on November 27, 2026 with `scripts/R/ficha_generica_v3.R --tarea CF_CONTAR_SILABAS`. Figures come from the data; the theoretical framework is shared by the tasks of the same construct. **Interpretation and team review are missing.** Spanish name: *Contar sílabas*. [Spanish version](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/auto/CF_CONTAR_SILABAS.html). ::: **In one sentence.** Syllable counting, from age 4 to 5 (5,786 administrations in 6 cohorts). Stability across time points ρ = .33. AUC .64–.66 against persistent reading difficulty. ## Description | | | |---|---| | Codes | 523 | | Battery | LEEDUCA | | Format | pictures on screen | | Items | 20 (523) according to the platform | | Task family | A · Accuracy | | Score | Correct responses | | Instructions (platform) | After naming the picture presented on the screen, the child counts the number of syllables in the word. | ## How it is programmed on the platform The platform is the reference: what the activity actually presents is what is measured. Configuration read from the activity itself on 22/10/2026 (without modifying it). Cell contents are in Spanish. | Code|Name on the platform |Presentation | Test items| Practice items|Example items |Time limit |Order |Scoring | Age.term (label 3)| |----:|:--------------------|:--------------------|----------:|--------------:|:-------------|:--------------|:-----|:--------|----------------------:| | 523|Contar sílabas |Imagen + botones 1–5 | 20| 0|caballo, tren |180 s en total |fijo |Aciertos | 4, 4.1, 4.2, 5, 5.1, 6| **Differences from the dictionary or the instructions (in Spanish):** - **523.** 20 ítems de 1 a 4 sílabas, sin ejemplo, con límite de 180 s. *Age.term: provisional reading of the activity's label 3 (3rd digit = age, 4th = term; 0 = annual), to be confirmed with the engineer.* **How it looks on the platform** (first item or example; 2026 screenshot; the interface is in Spanish). ::: {layout-ncol=1} ![523 · Contar sílabas](../../figuras/plataforma/523.jpg){.lightbox width="40%" fig-alt="Screenshot of activity 523"} ::: ## Theoretical framework Phonological awareness is the ability to reflect on and manipulate the sounds of speech. The platform's tasks cover a continuum of difficulty: - by **unit**: syllable or phoneme; - by **operation**: counting, identifying, segmenting or deleting; - by **position**: initial, final or any. The "all positions" version mixes items and is the most demanding. **What the evidence says:** - **Phonemes and manipulation are what most distinguish dyslexia.** In 2,252 children from six European languages, phoneme deletion and RAN were the strongest concurrent predictors of dyslexia [@landerl2013predictors]. In consistent orthographies, children with dyslexia perform below even younger readers of the same reading level on phoneme manipulation tasks, but not on syllable tasks [@parrila2020rlmatch]. - **In Spanish, phonological awareness develops in stages**, from the syllable to the phoneme. Phonemic awareness builds on learning to read and at the same time drives it: the relation is reciprocal [@denton2000pa]. Phonological awareness predicts above all the reading of complex syllables [@martinez2020silabica]. - **Its predictive value is universal, but changes with age.** Phonemic awareness, letters and RAN predict reading growth equally in Spanish, Czech and English [@caravolas2013growth]. Its relation with fluency, however, is more complex and depends on task and age, whereas RAN predicts fluency in all languages [@landerl2019pa]. This is what @catts2026definicion lead us to expect: precursors are useful for early prognosis and lose weight once there is reading to measure. The pilot task sheets develop this framework in more detail: [syllable counting](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/CF523.html) and [rapid naming](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/fichas/RAN.html) (*in Spanish*). **What our data show.** The pattern matches the literature: - **What predicts best.** Deletion tasks in all positions are those that best predict low Woodcock-Muñoz fluency (median AUC .72–.73, up to .81). - **In between.** The other deletion and identification tasks (.63–.68). - **What predicts least.** Phoneme segmentation and syllable counting (.60–.62). - **Consistency and stability.** Internal consistency is good (α = .82–.94), but stability between terms is low (ρ = .27–.41). Many tasks were given in only one or two sessions, and children change quickly at these ages. For an individual decision, the result should be confirmed at two time points. ## Sample and descriptive statistics | Time point| Cohort| Session|School year | N| Non-Preleo| Preleo| Schools| |----------:|------:|-------:|:-----------|---:|----------:|------:|-------:| | 4.1| 2011| 67|2015/16 | 928| 0| 928| 34| | 4.1| 2012| 154|2016/17 | 387| 387| 0| 17| | 4.1| 2013| 181|2017/18 | 575| 567| 8| 24| | 4.1| 2014| 625|2018/19 | 446| 49| 397| 20| | 4.1| 2015| 894|2019/20 | 495| 0| 495| 22| | 5.1| 2010| 66|2015/16 | 956| 261| 693| 36| | 5.1| 2011| 153|2016/17 | 904| 0| 904| 34| | 5.1| 2012| 182|2017/18 | 319| 315| 0| 16| | 5.1| 2013| 628|2018/19 | 776| 513| 263| 33| | Time point| N| Cohorts| Mean| SD| Median| Skewness| % floor| % ceiling| |----------:|-----:|----------------:|-----:|----:|------:|--------:|-------:|---------:| | 4.1| 1,003| 2012, 2013, 2014| 9.75| 5.21| 10| 0.02| 3.79| 2.89| | 5.1| 1,089| 2010, 2012, 2013| 13.61| 5.04| 14| -0.60| 0.18| 11.66| **Score range** (non-Preleo group, in correct responses). The usual range goes from P1 to P99 (98% of the children). The minimum–maximum is the one observed after cleaning; the possible range is 0–20 correct responses. | Time point| N|Usual range (P1–P99) |Min.–max. |Possible range | Warning| |----------:|-----:|:--------------------|:---------|:--------------|-------:| | 4.1| 1,003|0–20 |0–20 |0–20 | | | 5.1| 1,089|1–20 |0–20 |0–20 | | ## Reliability Stability across time points in the same children: ρ from .33–.40 (median .33, 3 pairs of time points). Internal consistency in the 2021 analyses: α = .86. | Cohort| From| To| n| r| ρ| |------:|----:|---:|---:|----:|----:| | 2011| 4.1| 5.1| 804| 0.33| 0.33| | 2012| 4.1| 5.1| 305| 0.40| 0.40| | 2013| 4.1| 5.1| 401| 0.35| 0.33| ## Validity **Concurrent.** With other tasks in its own domain (Phonological awareness), r = .40–.46. Outside its domain, the highest relation is with: Oral morphosyntax (4.1, r = .36); Oral morphosyntax (5.1, r = .29). **Against reading difficulty and comprehension.** Against persistent difficulty, AUC .64–.66. Against poor comprehension one or two school years later (non-circular criterion), AUC .57–.65. ![Validity: AUC with 95% confidence interval (labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_CONTAR_SILABAS_F2_validez.png){width=85%} **Against an external criterion, years later.** Against low Woodcock-Muñoz reading fluency in 2021/22 ([chapter](https://abarejo.github.io/leeduca-manual/criterio-woodcock.html), *in Spanish*), AUC .60–.61 (2 time points; 472–767 children). ## Provisional norms | Time point| N| Cohorts| P5| P10| P16| P25| P50| P75| P90| |----------:|-----:|----------------:|--:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:| | 4.1| 1,003| 2012, 2013, 2014| 1| 3| 4| 6| 10| 14| 17| | 5.1| 1,089| 2010, 2012, 2013| 4| 6| 8| 11| 14| 18| 20| These are norms by time point (school year × term). For dates between assessments and time points without a normative sample, study M3 proposes continuous norms on **months of instruction**, not on age, with relative age within the school year as an adjustment. ![Provisional norms (non-Preleo schools; labels in Spanish).](../../figuras/Ficha_auto_CF_CONTAR_SILABAS_F1_baremo.png){width=85%} ## Variables that affect it |Variable | Time point| n| Effect| p| |:---------------------------------------|----------:|-----:|------:|-----:| |School SES (ρ) | 4.1| 2,483| 0.124| 0.000| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 4.1| 2,653| 0.140| 0.000| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 4.1| 2,670| 0.227| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 4.1| 2,831| 0.185| | |School SES (ρ) | 5.1| 2,843| -0.020| 0.295| |Sex (d girl − boy; coding under review) | 5.1| 2,797| 0.054| 0.151| |Relative age (ρ with age in months) | 5.1| 2,790| 0.131| 0.000| |School (ICC) | 5.1| 2,955| 0.136| | ## For publications The LEEDUCA platform task “Syllable counting” (code 523; LEEDUCA battery) assesses syllable awareness (segmentation). Each item is presented with a picture on the screen; the examiner gives the instruction orally and records the child's response. It comprises 20 items. The time limit is 120 seconds. It is administered individually on a computer at school. In the 2010, 2011, 2012, 2013, 2014 and 2015 cohorts it was administered in 9 sessions, from 4 to 5 years of age. The main outcome is the number of correct responses. In our data (2021 analyses), internal consistency was α = .86 (N = 2,202, 20 items). Stability across successive administrations (median interval of 12 months) was ρ = .34 (median of 3 session pairs; range .32–.40). Stability across time points was ρ = .33–.40. Against later poor reading comprehension, AUC = .57–.65. ## Pending issues - Write the interpretation; review with the team.
